retention.stated: Choose your TTL. Default is 1 hour, max is 24 hours.
retention.notes: Default is 1 hour, max is 24 hours; no TTL specified defaults to `:1h`.

egress.terms: Unmetered and anonymous: blobs are 307-redirected to a presigned S3 URL (s3.us-east-1.storage.sh, X-Amz-Expires=1200), so bytes come off object storage, not the registry host. Range requests work.

record.tooling: Any distribution-spec client: oras, docker, skopeo, crane, regctl. Built on zot (per the repo: 'Zot runs an off-the-shelf image ghcr.io/project-zot/zot-linux-amd64 ... points zot at an S3-compatible bucket').
record.chaining: Any OCI artifact can be pushed with a TTL without auth, config or an account.
record.limits_note: TTL max 24h advertised (:5m/:1h/:6h/:24h), default 1h. Upload is slow (~11 MB/s observed: 1.5GB in 2m11s), so throughput is the practical per-connection cap. _catalog is blocked by nginx (401), tags/list is open.
record.reliability_note: Expiry is best-effort: the deployment repo states 'Tag expiry is handled separately and is not yet wired up in this repo', and open issue #151 reports images not expiring. Data WILL vanish at TTL; do not treat as durable. Intermittent connect timeouts observed from this network.
record.confidence_note: the ttl.sh page states the service is free forever with zero sign-up
